proof_summary: For an admissible integer, the even case follows from \(2\varphi(x)\le x\), while for odd \(x\) one writes \(v_2(\varphi(x))=\sum_{p\mid x}v_2(p-1)\): a non-Fermat-form prime factor yields the required product lower bound, and if all factors are Fermat primes then their distinct valuations are powers of two, so a sum at least \(2^{33}\) forces one valuation at least \(2^{33}\). That factor is either \(2^{2^{33}}+1\), excluded in the composite case, or already large enough; together with the direct totient values of the two proposed candidates, this proves minimality in both cases.
